parts.article:
The Development of Plastics
 
(A) The first plastics were developed as a substitute for natural rubber. Chemically, rubber is a polymer—a compound containing large molecules that are formed by the bonding of many smaller, simpler units, repeated over and over again. The same bonding principle—polymerization—is the basis of the creation of a huge range of plastics by the chemical industry. The first plastic was developed as a result of a competition in the USA. In the 1860s, $10,000 was offered to anybody who could replace ivory—supplies of which were declining—with something equally good as a material for making billiard balls. The prize was won by John Wesley Hyatt, with a material called celluloid. Celluloid was made by dissolving cellulose, a carbohydrate obtained from plants, in a solution of camphor dissolved in ethanol. This new material rapidly found other applications in the manufacture of everyday products such as knife handles and detachable collars and cuffs. But perhaps the best-known celluloid product was photographic film, without which the film industry could never have taken off at the end of the 19th century.
 
(B) Celluloid can be repeatedly softened and reshaped by heat, and is known as a thermoplastic. In 1907, Leo Baekeland (1863–1944), a Belgian chemist working in the USA, invented a different kind of plastic by causing phenol and formaldehyde to react together. Baekeland called it Bakelite, and it was the first of the thermosets—plastics that can be cast and moulded while hot, but cannot be softened by heat and reshaped once they have set. Bakelite was a good insulator, and was resistant to water and acid. With these properties it was soon being used in the manufacture of electrical switches as well as a variety of domestic items.
 
(C) As the century went on, the range of newly developed plastics increased. Chemists began looking for other small molecules that could be strung together to make polymers. In the 1930s, chemists in Britain discovered that the gas ethylene would polymerize under heat and pressure to form a thermoplastic they called polythene. Polypropylene followed in the 1950s. Both are used to make bottles, pipes and plastic bags. A small change in the starting material—replacing a hydrogen atom in ethylene with a chlorine atom—produced rigid PVC (polyvinyl chloride), a fireproof plastic suitable for drains and gutters. By adding certain chemicals, a soft form of PVC can be produced, suitable as a substitute for rubber in items such as waterproof clothing. A closely related plastic is Teflon or PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene). It produces very little friction, making it ideal for products such as non-stick frying pans.
 
(D) Polystyrene, a hard, clear material like glass, was developed during the 1930s in Germany, and its applications included food containers and toys. Expanded polystyrene is rigid and is widely used in packaging and insulation. Polyurethane, developed in the same country, was commonly produced as a foam, which was very useful in the production of insulating materials.
 
(E) In the 1930s, the first of the man-made fibres was created—nylon. Its inventor was a chemist called Wallace Carothers (1896–1937), who worked for the Du Pont company in the USA. He found that under the right conditions two particular chemicals would form a polymer that could be pumped out through holes and then stretched to form long glossy threads that could be woven like silk. Its first use was to make parachutes for the US armed forces in World War II. In the postwar years, it completely replaced silk in the manufacture of stockings. Many other synthetic fibres joined nylon, including Orlon, Acrilan, and Terylene. Today most garments are made of a blend of natural fibres, such as cotton and wool, and man-made fibres that make fabrics easier to look after.
 
(F) Despite its enormous usefulness, plastic has its drawbacks. In fact, one of its great strengths—its indestructibility—is its greatest disadvantage. Beaches all over the world, even on the remotest island, are littered with plastic bottles that nothing can destroy. Nor is it very easy to recycle plastics, as different types of plastic are often found in the same items and call for different treatments. Plastics can be made biodegradable by incorporating into their structure a material such as starch, which is attacked by bacteria and causes the plastic to fall apart. Other materials can be incorporated that gradually decay in sunlight—although bottles made of such materials have to be stored in the dark, to ensure they do not disintegrate before they have been used.

reference:
Q1

干扰 题目中的“Common uses”对应原文的“applications/products”，前面列举了billiard balls等，最后强调了最重要的一个。

句子 (Paragraph A) “But perhaps the best-known celluloid product was photographic film...”

解析 题目要求填Celluloid的一种常见用途，A段末尾提到也许最著名的赛璐珞产品是“photographic film（胶卷/摄影胶片）”，填 photographic film。

Q2

解析 题目要求填1907年美国发明的一种塑料名称，B段提到1907年Leo Baekeland发明了一种新塑料并称之为“Bakelite（胶木/酚醛塑料）”，填 Bakelite。

干扰 题目定位词是年份“1907”和国家“USA”，对应原文“In 1907... working in the USA... called it Bakelite”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “In 1907... Baekeland called it Bakelite...”

Q3

解析 题目要求填Bakelite的常见用途，B段末尾提到它很快被用于制造“electrical switches（电气开关）”以及各种家用物品，填 electrical switches。

干扰 “Household object”对应原文的“domestic items”，题目要填另一个并列的用途。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...it was soon being used in the manufacture of electrical switches as well as a variety of domestic items.”

Q4

干扰 题目问的是“Country of origin”，对应原文的“chemists in Britain”。

解析 题目要求填1930年代Polythene的原产国，C段提到1930年代“Britain（英国）”的化学家发现了聚乙烯，填 Britain。

句子 (Paragraph C) “In the 1930s, chemists in Britain discovered... polythene.”

Q5

解析 题目要求填Rigid PVC的性质，C段提到刚性PVC是一种“fireproof（防火）”塑料，适合做排水管，填 fireproof。

干扰 不能填 “a fireproof plastic”，因为表格中这一列只是填性质的。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...produced rigid PVC... a fireproof plastic suitable for drains and gutters.”

Q6

解析 题目说Polystyrene看起来像____，D段开头提到Polystyrene是一种坚硬、透明的材料，像“glass（玻璃）”，填 glass。

干扰 “Resembles”是“like”的同义替换。

句子 (Paragraph D) “Polystyrene, a hard, clear material like glass...”

Q7

句子 (Paragraph D) “Polyurethane... was commonly produced as a foam...”

干扰 “Usually manufactured as a...” 对应原文的 “commonly produced as a...”。

解析 题目说Polyurethane通常被制造为一种____，D段末尾说它通常被生产为一种“foam（泡沫）”，填 foam。

Q8

解析 题目说橡胶的化学结构与塑料“非常不同（very different）”。A段提到橡胶是聚合物，而同样的键合原理（polymerization）也是制造塑料的基础，暗示两者结构相似而非不同，选 FALSE。

干扰 原文强调“The same bonding principle... is the basis”，说明二者在化学基础上是同源的。

句子 (Paragraph A) “The same bonding principle—polymerization—is the basis of the creation of a huge range of plastics...”

Q9

解析 题目说John Wesley Hyatt是一位工业化学家。原文A段只说他赢得了奖金并开发了赛璐珞，从未提及他的职业头衔是“chemist（化学家）”，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 哪怕你知道历史背景，也要基于原文。文中明确称呼其他几位（Baekeland, Carothers）为chemist，唯独没提Hyatt的头衔。

句子 (Paragraph A) “The prize was won by John Wesley Hyatt...” (无职业描述)

Q10

句子 (Paragraph B) “Celluloid can be... softened... by heat... [Bakelite] cannot be softened by heat...”

解析 题目说赛璐珞和胶木对热的反应方式“相同（same way）”。原文B段明确对比：赛璐珞受热软化（thermoplastic），胶木受热不能软化（thermosets），反应相反，选 FALSE。

干扰 B段整段都在讲这两种塑料的热性质区别（Thermoplastic vs Thermosets）。

Q11

解析 题目说如果物体由多种塑料制成，就很难分解和再利用（recycle）。原文F段说回收不简单，因为“different types of plastic are often found in the same items（同一物品中常有不同塑料）”且需要不同处理，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Hard to break down and reuse” 对应 “Nor is it very easy to recycle”。

句子 (Paragraph F) “Nor is it very easy to recycle plastics, as different types of plastic are often found in the same items...”

Q12

解析 题目说向塑料中加入淀粉使其“更耐用（more durable）”。原文F段说加入淀粉是为了让其“biodegradable（可生物降解）”，导致塑料“fall apart（分解/散架）”，即变得不耐用，选 FALSE。

干扰 “Fall apart”和“biodegradable”是“durable”的反义概念。

句子 (Paragraph F) “...incorporating... starch, which is attacked by bacteria and causes the plastic to fall apart.”

Q13

解析 题目说设计用于分解的容器需要“特殊的储存条件（particular storage conditions）”。原文F段末尾提到光降解瓶子必须“stored in the dark（存放在黑暗中）”，以免提前分解，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Designed to decompose” 对应 “gradually decay in sunlight”，“Particular storage conditions” 对应 “stored in the dark”。

句子 (Paragraph F) “...bottles made of such materials have to be stored in the dark...”
